_comment: Machine source for RNVizion identity facts, the sibling of engine/brand.py. Brand tokens are colors and type; these are the facts about the person and the products. Same rule applies: import it, never hardcode. Change a fact HERE first, then run refresh_profile.py --all to find every surface that disagrees. ARCHIVES: docs/eval-history/ preserves dated eval reports and must keep retired phrases verbatim; retirement checks skip it wholesale via ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE in refresh_profile.py, and the ledger prints that exclusion every sweep. No per-phrase exemptions are needed there, ever -- if a future retirement fails under docs/eval-history/, the checker regressed; do not add an exemption to quiet it.
_resumes_out_of_scope: 2026-08-12, v1.3.0. The .docx resume variants are PERSONAL documents, handed directly to people, and they carry the personal cell. They are deliberately not modelled here: no appears_in list names them, no fact claims to appear on them, and nothing in this manifest describes their contents. This is a scope decision, not an oversight -- do not re-add 'resumes' to an appears_in list. TWO DIFFERENT ARTIFACTS SHARE THE WORD: resume/index.html in rnvizion.github.io is the PUBLIC web resume, it carries no phone number, and it stays fully checked -- see facts.eval_cases.sources. Verify the one that serves. scripts/refresh_profile.py --docx still exists as a local, opt-in, recordless tool a human can point at their own files; it stores nothing and no workflow passes that flag.

identity._phone_removed: 2026-08-12, v1.3.0. identity.phone held the personal cell and this file is public and machine-readable at scale. Removed from HEAD; it does not come back. DO NOT re-add a personal number under any key in this manifest -- not hashed, not partial, not commented out: ten digits is 10^10 candidates and roughly 10^7 with a known area code, so a hash here would be obfuscation wearing the costume of a control. The publishable number is identity.brand_phone below. NOTE THE COUPLING: generate_contact_card.py in rnvizion.github.io keys a tripwire on the path (identity, phone). That path is now deliberately empty and must stay empty; re-populating it is what the tripwire exists to catch.

brand_phone._comment: Brand routing number (Google Voice, created 2026-08-10), published on /card/ and going to print. A DIFFERENT FACT from the personal cell, which is not in this manifest at all -- do not merge them, and do not add a key that could be read as either. Both forms are carried rather than derived: the card face takes display, the tel: href and the vCard TEL take e164, and a consumer deriving one from the other is a consumer inventing a format. NO CHECKER READS THIS YET. It lands so consumers stop hardcoding it; a source-backed guard for it is open work and this comment comes out when that guard exists.

facts._comment: Values on more than one surface that have drifted before. 'sources' are files the checker reads; 'appears_in' is the wider map including surfaces it cannot reach. 'match' is the literal phrase that must appear on those sources -- a bare value is a useless needle ("60" matches a CSS font weight), so where a fact is printed inside a phrase, give the phrase. MOVE 'match' WITH 'value': a stale match fails loudly on the next run, which is correct but surprising if you forget the pairing.

derive.note: Source 'def test_' count is a floor: parametrized tests expand at runtime. The checker verifies the displayed floor is actually supported by source, and says when the next rung on the ladder has been earned. SUBSET: rnv-publishing-agent and rnv-brand are not counted, so the floor is conservative by construction. Adding a repo to this list requires recomputing floor_observed in the same change.

tests._floor_observed_note: REFRESHED 2026-08-17, 4908 -> 5131. This is a recorded observation, not a target: it is what the eight listed repos derived on the day it was measured, and it moves whenever they gain tests. The PUBLISHED value stays '5,000+' -- the floor rising does not oblige the prose to follow, and 5,131 supports it more comfortably than 4,908 did. The next rung is 5,500, and the checker will say so when source earns it rather than when someone feels like claiming it.
tests._comment: Public surfaces carry a floor that steps in 5k increments, not an exact count. The exact figure came from a CI run and cannot be re-derived without running every suite; the floor can be, from source. Move the display to the next rung only when the source floor clears it.

eval_cases.note: Total only on public surfaces; the split is never published. A trap flipping out_of_corpus -> in_corpus on publication moves the split without moving the total, so the split fails the publication test and lives here as a machine-checked fact instead.

derive.note: Exactly derivable: one JSON object per line, each carrying a 'kind'. Frozen at 60 by decision 2026-08-05; update split in the same commit as any trap flip. CORRECTED 2026-08-17 from 38/22 to 39/21, and the correction is this check working exactly as the note above predicts: a trap flipped out_of_corpus -> in_corpus in the corpus repo, the TOTAL stayed at 60, and no published surface moved. Nothing but this machine-checked split could have caught it, which is precisely why the split lives here rather than on a page. The flip itself is the corpus chat's to explain; this manifest records only what the file now holds.

eval_thresholds._comment: The three gates. Declared in rnv-ask-the-corpus/eval/thresholds.json, carried here, and quoted in prose on the resume page. check_thresholds verifies this manifest against the source file; verify_threshold_prose verifies the page against this manifest, so the chain runs source -> manifest -> surface with no unverified hop. CLOSED 2026-08-16, and the original note here was wrong about why: it said adding 'thresholds' to the site repo would 'fail spuriously' because the dispatch looks for eval/thresholds.json. It would not fail -- check_thresholds returns early on a missing file, so it would run, find nothing, and PASS having verified nothing. Quieter and worse than the failure predicted, and the reason the fix is a separate check rather than an extra entry in a checks array.

prose._comment: THE NEEDLE IS THE PHRASE, NOT THE NUMBER, and the direction word is the reason. `85%` matches anything on the page, and flipping 'at or above' to 'at or below' leaves the number intact while inverting the gate -- the value would still agree and the sentence would be a lie. {value} is substituted from the figure above, so the phrase and the value cannot drift apart here the way they can in prose. A phrase that no longer matches is a FAILURE and not a skip: it means the page was reworded, and a check that quietly stops finding its needle is a check that verifies nothing while reporting clean.

expiring_surfaces._comment: Surfaces that go stale on a calendar rather than on a change. This is NOT a facts entry: facts assert that a surface matches a derived value, and this asserts that a date is still comfortably ahead of today. There is nothing to derive it from -- the file IS the source -- so the check is a comparison against now. Note the consequence: this is the one check that fires while the surface is still CORRECT. That is deliberate; by the time it is wrong it is too late, because nothing else will ever prompt a refresh, and it is why the Monday schedule is load-bearing rather than a convenience. WIRED 2026-08-16 by verify_expiring, which runs unconditionally in the facts pass -- not as a CHECKS key, because each entry carries its own repo and a new registry key runs on zero surfaces until fourteen manifest entries opt in. IT ASSERTS TWO THINGS AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT GETS FORGOTTEN: that the date is ahead of now, and that the file's date still MATCHES the value below. A margin measured against a figure nobody updated is a margin against nothing. The previous note here said nothing read this block; that was true for seven days and is now false.

.well-known/security.txt.reason: RFC 9116 makes Expires mandatory. An expired security.txt reads as an abandoned project, which is a worse signal than having no file at all. Weekly profile-drift gives roughly eight warnings before the fail window, which is enough notice to act without the warning becoming noise.

phone_exemptions._comment: Bounded exactly like the retirement exemptions, and deliberately WITHOUT a value field. Naming a number here to permit it would publish it, which is the failure this whole block exists to prevent. A path and a count are enough: occurrence two has to be a deliberate edit. Keyed on repo as well as path, because a bare relative path is ambiguous across fourteen repos and the retirement ledger already carries that ambiguity. NEVER write an example number into a reason string here -- the manifest audit reads its own prose and will trip on it, correctly.

coupled_manual_work._comment: A PROMPT, NEVER A GUARD. Every check in this system answers 'does this disagree?'; this answers 'did you just make something stale?' -- a different question at a different moment. It does not verify the manual work happened and must never claim to: the moment it does, it is a construct that looks like enforcement and is not, which is the failure this project has caught four times. It cannot fail the job, and the honest cost of that is that it can be ignored. KEYED ON THE TRIGGER, not on where the stale thing lives -- what a push can see is which files in THIS repo changed. A coupling whose trigger is in another repository needs a workflow there; rnv-live's three-file font change is the one in that state today. This is what manual_surfaces was missing: its cadences are 'attached to an existing event' and nothing made the event fire.

If a mark ruling moved: type_register in profile.json is the machine-readable half and verify_type compares against it, not against this document.

type_register._comment: Machine-readable half of BRAND_TYPE.md, for verify_type. The REASONING lives in the register and is not repeated here -- this block holds only what a checker can compare. Change a value here and change BRAND_TYPE.md in the same commit, or the two documents in this repo disagree and the source is what a reader trusts.

mark_tracking._comment: Expected letter-spacing per mark selector. KEYED ON SELECTOR BECAUSE THE SELECTOR IS THE ROLE -- the same reason the mark needs a class discriminator at all. rnv-live's mark is 0.09em at 1.05rem because it is a nav mark by role, not because of its size, and a guard cannot infer role from contents. THE MAPPING HOLDS ONLY WHILE EACH SELECTOR IS USED AT ONE SIZE CLASS: put a .logo at display size and selector stops standing in for role, and this block has to split. Values are what every surface ships today, verified across all fourteen marks. Written with a leading zero for readability; the check parses the number, because `.06em` and `0.06em` are the same value written two ways and a string compare would report drift where none exists. The three raster generators are outside this entirely -- PIL, no markup, 1.8px absolute, held true by a three-file coupling and nothing else.

mark_selectors._comment: THE MARK IS A ROLE AND TEXT ALONE CANNOT IDENTIFY IT. The brand name also appears as an author byline on eight blog files, in page titles, and in the footer's long form; those are mentions of the name, not renderings of the mark, and the register's Labels row permits them in mono. A class list is required alongside the exact-text test because a check cannot infer the role from the contents -- the contents are the brand name either way. Same argument as F13's single-member allowlist: an inferred scope is a hole.

no_canonical_link._comment: Pages the register exempts from the shared font-link string, so the link-drift check does not report a decision as drift. THE RULE IS: a page requests every face it draws and no face it doesn't; the chrome pages share one string only because they happen to draw all five. /card/ requests only the three faces and four weights it draws. aiii/ had Montserrat trimmed on 2026-08-15 because it draws no mark -- it has no site nav, and its own AIII wordmark is mono. It still DECLARES --font-mark per decision #18, so the five-token vocabulary is identical on every page; declaring a token costs nothing and keeps a guard reading one shape everywhere. Each entry here is a decision recorded in BRAND_TYPE.md, not a value tolerated.
